punchline: The students graded only on how many photos they took ended up taking the best ones.
thirty_sec: A photography professor, Jerry Uelsmann, split his class in two. One group was graded only on how many photos they took. The other had to turn in one near-perfect photo. At the end of the term, the best photos all came from the quantity group. They'd spent months shooting, experimenting and learning from mistakes, while the quality group mostly theorised. James Clear calls this the difference between motion, meaning planning, and action, the behaviour that actually produces results.
question: In that photo class, would you have joined the one-perfect-shot group or the shoot-as-much-as-you-can group, and is that same instinct what's holding you back now?
